newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan warlord deploys troops amid Taleban talks.
newsitem.headline: Afghan warlord deploys troops amid Taleban talks.

text.p: Afghanistan's ruling Taleban movement held more peace talks on Thursday with powerful northern warlord Abdul Rashid Dostum as he sent his troops to face Taleban north of Kabul.

The Islamic militia, which controls two-thirds of the country, says the ethnic Uzbek general has pledged to stay out of fighting between Taleban and the government it ousted from Kabul three weeks ago.
The meeting in the southern Afghan town of Kandahar decided to continue talks brokered by neighbouring Pakistan, Taleban sources told Reuters.
Pakistani Interior Minister Naseerullah Babar attended Thursday's talks as he did on Wednesday, when two ministers of Taleban government met Dostum in the northern town of Mazar-i-Sharif.
A three-man delegation sent by Dostum met Taleban officials for about two hours before returning to Mazar-i-Sharif, the sources said.
"The talks were positive and held in a cordial atmosphere," Taleban spokesman Maulvi Mohammad Haqqani said. "We are hopeful that an understanding will be reached with Dostum."
He gave no details of the talks, which Taleban sources said were aimed at bringing peace to the war-shattered country.
Earlier on Thursday, a Taleban government spokesman said in Kabul that the Taleban had been assured by Dostum that he would not join in the fighting north of the capital.

"He has assured us," acting information minister Amir Khan Mutaqi told Reuters after reports surfaced that Dostum had sent forces south to join those of former government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood.
"If he does join in the fighting, it will be his decision," Mutaqi said without elaboration.
On Wednesday, Taleban Foreign Minister Mulla Mohammed Ghous held talks with Dostum, who has perhaps the most potent single armed force in Afghanistan.

Mutaqi said the Taleban were satisfied with the talks, whose aim "was to persuade the northern movement not to make friendship with those forces who have been expelled and isolated by the people", a reference to Masood.

"About this issue, the northern movement has given us assurances. We are satisfied with them. We will have more talks in this regard and our concern is to a great degree about Dostum's involvement in the fighting," Mutaqi said.
Shortly before he spoke, Dostum General Abdul Majid Ruzi told reporters in Jabal os-Siraj at the mouth of the Salang Pass through the Hindu Kush mountains that Uzbek forces were being sent south.

"As you know, the (Afghan Defence) Council decided that if there was an attack, all the forces would come together and we would insert our troops and our tanks and our artillery into the line and we have," Ruzi said.
Uzbek forces were heading south of Jabal os-Siraj towards the town of Charikar, a 30-minute drive south and just north of the front line between the Taleban and Masood's forces.
"We came from the Salang and we're going to Kabul. We're going to bash the Taleban today," said one Uzbek soldier on the way south.
